newsitem.title: BOSNIA: British defence secretary visits Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: British defence secretary visits Bosnia.

text.p: British Defence Secretary George Robertson met officers of the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia on Tuesday, a day after Britain cast doubt on a July 1998 deadline for pulling alliance troops out of the country.

In his first visit to Bosnia as the new Labour government's defence secretary, Robertson held talks with U.S. General William Crouch, commander of the multinational Stabilisation Force (SFOR), to discuss efforts to build a lasting peace, SFOR spokesmen said.

Robertson's visit coincides with growing frustration among Western powers with Bosnian Moslem, Serb and Croat political leaders who have failed to reunify the country under terms of the Dayton peace treaty.
British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook warned on Monday that the political paralysis may require an extension of the NATO-led mission to avoid a return to war.
U.S. officials have insisted that the date cannot be changed and that the 31,000-strong force will be withdrawn by then.
The Dayton treaty ended the 1992-95 conflict but the country remains divided into separate ethnic communities ruled by nationalist political parties.

Robertson held talks with the president of the country's Serb republic, Biljana Plavsic, in the northwestern town of Banja Luka on Monday. He was due to meet members of the collective presidency on Tuesday afternoon in Sarajevo.
He also visited British troops troops stationed in the Banja Luka region on Monday and observed an artillery firing exercise by the 4th Regiment Royal Artillery in the western town of Glamoc.
